entry.label: Graduation at Marburg
entry.source_text: Bernard Andreae graduated from Marburg in 1956 under Friedrich Matz, specializing in Roman sarcophagi; his thesis analyzed historical motifs within sarcophagus iconography.

entry.label: Assistant at German Archaeological Institute, Italy
entry.source_text: From 1956 to 1959, he served as Assistant at the German Archaeological Institute in Italy.

entry.label: Studien zur roemischen Grabkunst
entry.source_text: In 1962, he completed his habilitation in Bonn with a monograph on Roman funerary art ("Studien zur roemischen Grabkunst"), dedicated to his mentors Friedrich Matz, Reinhard Herbig, and Ernst Langlotz.

entry.label: Esquiline fresco cycle
entry.source_text: Between 1960 and 1970, he published studies on painting and sculpture, including the Esquiline fresco cycle (1962), the Aldobrandini Wedding (1962), and imitation vs. originality in 3rd-century AD sarcophagi (1970).

entry.label: Professor at Bochum
entry.source_text: This work absorbed him during his tenure as professor at Bochum (1965-1977) and Marburg (from 1978), until his appointment as Director of the German Archaeological Institute in Rome in 1984 (until 1995).

entry.label: Excavation at Tiberius's Villa in Sperlonga
entry.source_text: In the 1970s and 1980s, he tracked the Rome Soprintendenza's excavations at Tiberius's Villa in Sperlonga, producing complex reconstructions of the Hellenistic-Roman sculpture groups.

entry.label: Alexander Mosaic
entry.source_text: His contributions to Neue Forschungen in Pompeji (1974) and a new edition of the Alexander Mosaic (1977) reflect his focus on Roman painting and Late Republican/Early Imperial classicism.

entry.source_text: Since 1974, he has edited the Roman sarcophagi corpus "Die antiken Sarkophagreliefs", authoring the 1980 volume on hunting scenes ("Die römischen Jagdsarkophage": https://digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/diglit/asr1_2 ).
